title: Service catalog and inventory — operational notes
content:
Purpose
-----
Quick working notes on the service catalog + cluster inventory that will feed inference routing decisions across regions and deployment modes. This is intended as an operational design doc (brainstorm -> implementation checklist) rather than a final architecture spec.

Goals / constraints
- Provide a single source-of-truth (catalog) for node capabilities that is small, queryable, and tolerant to transient state.
- Fast lookups for routing (sub-10ms reads for hot paths), but also strong provenance for capacity planning and audits.
- Support multi-region affinity + graceful fallback (e.g., prefer region A, fallback to compatible instance in region B, then to lower-tier GPU).
- Keep labeling low-friction for infra automation (labels should be machine-friendly, stable, and compact).
- Avoid excessive cardinality in labels — routing performance degrades with too many distinct tags.

High level components
- Node advertiser (agent): emits periodic lightweight heartbeat with capability snapshot to control plane.
- Inventory service (catalog): time-series + latest-state store. Exposes a read API for routing decisions and a write ingestion API for agent/telemetry.
- Health aggregator: calculates current health score from raw signals and attaches reason tags (eg: high-memory-pressure).
- Model compatibility index: small service that maps model artifact -> required capability vector (e.g., min-ptx, memory, compute class, kernel variants).
- Router (policy engine): consumes inventory + model-index + runtime policy to produce ranked candidate nodes.

Labeling taxonomy (recommendation)
- node.env: prod | staging | dev
- node.region: e.g. us-west1, eu-central1
- node.pool: dedicated-longrunning | burstable | preemptible
- gpu.family: a100 | h100 | a10 | t4
- gpu.memory_gb: numeric string (e.g., "40") — used for quick numeric comparisons in policy layer
- gpu.arch_rev: sm80 | sm89 | sm90 (helps pick CUDA/kernel variants)
- nvlink: true | false (if available)
- storage.local_ssd: nvme | sata | none  (important for embedding caches)
- container.runtime: containerd | nvidia-docker | singularity  (for edge/on-prem special cases)
- tags.experimental: free-form short list for ops notes (avoid for routing)

Why keep gpu.family + arch separate?
- kernel selection and quantization behavior often depends on family + arch_rev. Splitting makes matching policies less brittle when we roll new micro-variants.

Health signals (raw and derived)
Raw (emitted at ~10s cadence from agent):
- heartbeat_ts (unix ms)
- cpu_load_1m (float)
- mem_used_gb, mem_total_gb
- gpu_util_pct per GPU index (serialized as CSV string)
- gpu_mem_used_mb per GPU index
- nvlink_errors (count)
- disk_io_ms_p50, disk_io_ms_p95
- recent_ooms (count last 1h)
- ssh_last_success (timestamp) — for private/on-prem verification
- running_tasks_count, pending_tasks_count

Derived (aggregated by health aggregator):
- availability: up | degraded | offline  (rules below)
- health_score: 0-100 (higher is better) — simple weighted sum but stored for auditability
- hot_kv_hit_ratio: number (0-1) — helps select cache-optimized nodes
- failure_reason_tags: list (e.g., ["oom_recent", "kernel_compiler_mismatch"])

Availability scoring (first-pass heuristic)
- If heartbeat_ts older than 30s -> offline
- If recent_ooms > 0 or nvlink_errors > 5 in last 10m -> degraded (health_score -= 30)
- If gpu_util_pct median > 88% for last 60s -> degraded
- If disk_io_ms_p95 > 200ms -> degrade score (affects embedding workloads)
- Baseline health_score calculation: 100 - (cpu_penalty + mem_penalty + gpu_penalty + disk_penalty + recent_failure_penalty)

Inventory storage model (practical recommendation)
- Primary: small document store keyed by node_id containing latest state (labels + last_heartbeat + health_score + capacity_vector). Low-latency reads optimized via in-memory cache (Redis or Memcached).
- Events/Time-series: raw heartbeats are appended to a TSDB (Influx/Prometheus remote write or Bigtable) for history, anomaly detection, and audits.
- Backfill pipeline: agents should also push to an events topic (Kafka) to allow replay and downstream consumers.

API contract (readable keys example)
- GET /inventory/v1/nodes?region=us-west1&gpu_family=a100&min_memory_gb=40 -> returns ordered list of node_ids + short metadata (labels, health_score, last_heartbeat).
- GET /inventory/v1/node/{node_id} -> detailed doc (labels, recent metrics pointers, running_tasks_count).

Routing policy primitives
- locality_preference: same_region | adjacent_region | any_region
- cost_tier: premium | standard | discounted
- required_labels: exact matches for node labels
- soft_negative_tags: prefer nodes without these tags
- capacity_reserve: number tokens to leave free for high-priority traffic (configurable per model)
- model_compatibility_filter: use model-index to drop incompatible nodes early

Multi-region fallbacks (simple flow)
1) Try same-region nodes matching required_labels sorted by health_score and cost_tier.
2) If capacity insufficient within latency SLO, expand to adjacent-region set and re-rank with latency penalty.
3) Final fallback: degrade model variant (lower memory / quantized) via model-compatibility index and re-run matching in preferred region set.

Important practical tradeoffs / notes
- Don’t keep all labels in routing queries. Instead, compile a compact capability vector (bitmask or short tag) that routing can compare quickly. High-cardinality labels (like 'owner:team-name') are useful for inventory UIs but harmful in policy engine.
- Keep the hot read path cache-only for milliseconds. Use write-through invalidation from agent -> cache on heartbeat. Occasional stale reads are acceptable (we accept brief mismatch at routing time).
- For private/on-prem nodes we need a separate verifier to assert identity of agent heartbeats (mutual TLS + signed attestations).
- Agents must fall back to beacon-only mode if they cannot reach control plane for extended period; tag their last_known_state with a nonce so router can detect stale but authenticated nodes.

Operational checklist (next steps)
- [ ] Finalize label set and register as single source-of-truth in infra repo (owners: @rileyg, @maya).
- [ ] Implement health_aggregator prototype that consumes agent heartbeats and emits health_score. (JIRA-PLAT-498)
- [ ] Short perf test for inventory read latency with 100k nodes (target p99 < 8ms) — create load harness.
- [ ] Wire model-compatibility index with current model catalog; create migration for older model tags.
- [ ] Draft runbook: what to do when health_score drops across an AZ (auto-drain? traffic diversion?).

Open questions / unknowns
- How to represent multi-GPU topology in labels succinctly? (we currently serialize per-GPU arrays but need a compact summary for routing). Proposal: add gpu.sockets and gpu.count labels plus topology_hint: nvlink-ring | no-nvlink.
- Do we want per-request node reservation for latency-critical requests? (adds complexity and leftover capacity fragmentation).
- How to surface topology-dependent kernel variants in model-compat index without exploding combinatorics? (we can prioritize families + arch_rev and keep explicit overrides for special models).

Notes to self / informal TODOs
- sketch of a heartbeat payload (put into platform-inventory repo)
- follow up with SRE on log retention for TSDB (cost implications)
- sync with product-hosted-api to ensure routing API supports per-route capacity_reserve and fallback thresholds

Appendix: example heartbeat payload (pseudo-JSON, compact)
{
  node_id: "node-aws-usw2-az1-1234",
  ts: 1700000000000,
  labels: "node.region=us-west1;node.pool=dedicated-longrunning;gpu.family=a100;gpu.count=8;gpu.memory_gb=40",
  metrics: "gpu_util=12,8,9,14,7,11,3,2;cpu_load_1m=0.82;mem_used_gb=56;mem_total_gb=256",
  recent_failures: "oom:0;nvlink:0",
  signature: "<agent-signed-payload>"
}

End of notes.
